This petition is filed by the petitioners-accused Nos.1 and 2 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the entire criminal proceedings in CC No.2891/2020 arising out of Crime No.29/2017 registered by Seshadripuram Police, Bengaluru and charge-sheeted for the offence punishable under Section 7 of the Specified Bank Notes (Cessation of Liabilities) Act, 2017 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act' for short).

sentences.text:
Heard Sri Kiran S. Javali, learned senior counsel for the petitioners and Smt. M.M. Waheeda,
learned HCGP for the respondent-State.

3. The case of the prosecution is that the CCB police inspector, one Dr. B.S. Sudhakar, filed a complaint against the petitioners alleging that on 19.03.2017, he found one Maruthi 800 car bearing registration No.KA-02- N-7015 standing near Seshadripuram, containing the old currency notes.
When on suspicion, it was inspected two persons were found keeping a sum of Rs.1,28,00,000/- of various denominations of old notes, which were demonetized by the Government of India in the year 2016.

4. Accordingly, FIR has been registered for the offences punishable under Section 7 of the Act as well as Section 420 of IPC and after the investigation, the police filed the charge-sheet only for the offence punishable under Section 7 of the Act.
Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioners are before this Court.

Learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner contended that the alleged offence punishable under Section 7 of the Act is punishable only with fine or five times of the face value of the notes as penalty.
The offences are non-cognizable one.
Therefore, without prior permission of the Magistrate under Section 155(2) of Cr.P.C., the FIR cannot be registered and the police cannot file the charge sheet.

He has also contended that the FIR was registered on 19.03.2017, whereas, the charge-sheet was filed on 04.12.2019, there is a delay of two years 9 months in taking cognizance for the offence punishable under Section 7 of the Act and therefore, there is a bar for taking cognizance.
Hence, he prays for quashing the criminal proceedings.
6. Learned HCGP objected the petition.

7. Upon hearing the arguments of learned senior counsel for the petitioners and the learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent-State and on perusal of records, it is seen that FIR was registered on NC: 2024:KHC:45751 19.03.2017 for the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC.
For filing of FIR for the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC, permission is not required as Section 420 of IPC is a cognizable offence.

However, on careful reading of the contents of the FIR,
there is no ingredients made out for the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC.
Therefore, the police cleverly added Section 420 of IPC in order to avoid taking permission under Section 155 (2) of Cr.P.C. from the Magistrate.
That apart, the charge-sheet has been filed only for the offence punishable under Section 7 of the Act, which is punishable only with fine.

As per Schedule - II of the Cr.P.C., the offences punishable upto three years, other than the IPC are non-cognizable offences,
therefore, the offences alleged in the charge-sheet is non-cognizable offence and without permission of the Magistrate taking cognizance and filing charge-sheet by the police is not sustainable under the law.
As per Section 468 (2)(a) of Cr.P.C. if the offence punishable is only with fine, the period of limitation for taking cognizance is six months.

In the NC: 2024:KHC:45751 instant case, the FIR was registered on 19.03.2017 and the charge-sheet has been filed on 04.12.2019, after lapse of more than two years nine months for taking the cognizance itself, which is barred by limitation under Section Sri Jemmi Rahu V K vs The State-Through The Police Inspector on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127761612/
3 468 (2)(a) of Cr.P.C.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER i. Petition is allowed.
ii.

The proceedings against the petitioners-accused Nos.1 and 2 in C.C.No.2891/2020 arising out of Crime No.29/2017 pending on the file of the I Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Bangalore registered by Seshadripuram Police Station and charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Section 7 of the Specified Bank Notes (Cessation of Liabilities) Act, 2017 is hereby quashed.
